title: a password change or reset leaves the account's other sessions live
description:
## BLUF

A successful password change does not revoke the account's other sessions, and neither does the reset
flow. Raised from gate59's review of PR #1382 (KS 1005). **Pre-existing — not introduced by that PR.**

## N-1382-1 — no session revocation on a successful password change

A successful change makes **zero** `revokeAllUserSessions` calls. The reset flow does not revoke
either. So after a password change — including a change prompted by suspected compromise — every
other authenticated session on that account stays live.

Scope of the evidence, stated so it is not over-read: this was **measured on mocked calls only**, not
against a running stack. The count of zero is a count of calls the handler makes, not a live
observation of a surviving session.

## N-1382-2 — the e2e test for this can never fail

- [ ] Fix the e2e case so it can fail. Case 12.5.3, "other sessions should be invalidated", POSTs to
      `/api/auth/change-password` — **a route that does not exist** — and asserts only inside
      `if (status === 200)`. Because the request cannot return 200, the assertion body never runs, so
      the test passes unconditionally. It has therefore never tested the behaviour in N-1382-1, and
      the correct route is the one KS 1005 fixes.

## Adjacent, and deliberately not merged into this ticket

KS 257 ("Session revocation only enforced at the auth service") is adjacent but different — it is
about *where* revocation is enforced, not *whether* a password change triggers it — and it is
archived. Noted here so the connection is not lost.

nodes.title: Refs KS-1407: e2e case 12.5.3 calls the real change-password route, on its own account
Refs KS-1407: a password change and a password reset revoke the account's sessions

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** N-1382-2 is raised as PR 2016 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2016), head `d91821a99dbbdadf83854b78dc5cebaeec1cbc99`, built on develop `5fc5569ed96a`, READY FOR GATE (tier 2). NOT RUN: the e2e case needs a running stack. Not merged, not deployed.

- **What changes:** case 12.5.3 in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/security-bad-actor.prelaunch.spec.ts`.
  - It now calls `POST /api/users/me/change-password`, and a non-200 fails the case.
  - It runs on its own throwaway account, `e2e-ks1407-<uuid>` (domain example.com), with random strong passwords. That is Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-05: the shared seeded accounts' passwords are below the route's 12-character minimum, so a change back is refused.
  - Session A must answer 401 on `GET /api/users/me` after the change.
- **Each run leaves one labelled account** on the stack it runs against; it is not deleted, the same as the other register callers in the e2e suite.
- **Checked without a stack:**
  - the dead route under `tests/e2e`: 0 (develop 2); the code-form `if (changePwRes.status === 200) {`: 0 (develop 1);
  - a type check of the spec: 0 errors, and a planted error is reported;
  - no eslint config covers `tests/e2e`, so lint did not run.
- **Gate note N1 is already on develop** (comment a9b40dc6). With this PR merged and run, nothing is left on this ticket. The ticket stays In Progress until the case has run green on a stack and the change is deployed.

**BLUF:** Correction to the 2026-11-04 comment: gate note N1 is NOT open. It is already on develop, as commit 21e2ffd20 (`Refs KS-1692: a revoke that THROWS maps onto the same post-write 503`), an ancestor of develop 5fc5569ed96a. Only N-1382-2 (the e2e case) is left on this ticket.

- **Code at develop 5fc5569ed96a:** both password doors wrap `revokeAllUserSessions` in a try that re-throws a `ServiceUnavailableError` (503). Change-password is `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:1025-1035`; reset is `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:922-936`.
- **Cells at develop:** `ks1407-change-password-refuses-when-the-store-cannot-revoke`, `ks1407-reset-password-refuses-when-the-store-cannot-revoke` and `ks1868-auth-reset-password-revoke-unreadable-throw` pass 18 of 18. The first run skipped all 18 on a cold-import hook timeout at load about 6; the rerun at load 5 was green.
- **N1's own mutant**, `.catch(() => 0)` on the revoke call, each one type-checked (tsc rc 0), every kill by assertion: change-password door killed by 2 cells; reset door killed by 4; both doors killed by 6. Restored byte-equal.
- **N-1382-2** is being fixed in its own PR, `Refs KS-1407`, on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-05: e2e case 12.5.3 will call the real route, `POST /api/users/me/change-password`.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1655 merged as 86df4f5a52cc on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115. Verified by git at ee1e1b832115, not observed live. Left open: N-1382-2 and gate note N1, as comment 4d6333ed records.

- **In the deployed tree:** 38 of the squash's 41 added non-test lines are present verbatim at ee1e1b832115 (control: 8 of them were already present at its parent), so the change both password doors make (revoke the account's other sessions, fail closed when the session store cannot revoke) is in the deployed source, with later edits to 3 lines.
- **Still open:** N-1382-2 is untouched, and gate BS1's note N1 is a residual gap (comment 4d6333ed).

## BLUF
**MERGED to `develop` as `86df4f5a52cc36b40276b441900627bf0a4c5de5` (squash of PR #1655), verified at source.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions and both fail closed when the session store cannot revoke. Gate BS1 (Opus, tier 1, DELTA round 2 of 2) returned GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers, 5 notes. **KS-1407 stays OPEN: N-1382-2 is untouched, and gate note N1 is a real residual gap.** Not deployed.

## Verified at source, not from the merge response
- merge sha `86df4f5a52cc36b40276b441900627bf0a4c5de5`; **tree `2346900a5105fe24f8b3777a73123dd6df80a2a5`**, equal to the landing the gate and the GO both predicted and to my own `merge-tree` figure;
- **exactly ONE parent**, `f4259b8ed3875316a269d3228031c198eec39edd`, which was `develop` at the GO;
- 8 files, **+775/-3**; subject 82 characters; **0 attribution trailers**; `develop`'s tip is now this commit.

## What landed
`revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0 without throwing** when the store is unreachable, while `createSession` throws in the same condition. The first landing therefore wrote the password, burned the single-use reset token and answered 200 while revoking nothing, and the old sessions validated again once Redis recovered. Both routes now confirm the revocation is possible **before** the write and **re-assert after** it, because a pre-write check alone is a check-then-act.

Route-local, using the already-exported `isRedisAvailable`, so `revokeAllUserSessions` keeps its contract for its two other callers. The refusals differ on purpose: reset leaves the token unburned; change-password says the password **WAS** changed.

**Change-password revokes the caller's own session**, so the client must sign in again. No in-repo client calls either route — measured, with controls.

## Residual, and why this ticket does not close
- **N-1382-2** untouched: the e2e case posts to `/api/auth/change-password`, a route that does not exist.
- **Gate note N1 (MEDIUM), my own declared gap A5:** a revocation that **throws** after the write is fail-closed on reset (500, token kept, the retry works) but only half fail-closed on change-password — the password **is** written, an old session is **ACTIVE** after recovery, and the caller is told only "unexpected error". My `.catch(() => 0)` arm reds **0 of the 23** cells; the gate's own probes kill it. Recorded on KS-1692 with the gate's fix shape, for a later tier-1 round.
- **N2 (LOW-MEDIUM):** `session.ts:323`'s unguarded `del` can orphan the remaining sessions mid-loop. Also on KS-1692.
- **N4 (mine, trivial):** change-password's post-write 503 advises signing in again although that path leaves the caller's own session alive, and two of my comments cite `:317-318`/`:156` where the head has `:316`/`:155`. Both ride the KS-1692 round, on the gate's instruction, rather than a new PR.
- Tickets filed from the gate's notes: **KS-1690**, **KS-1691**, **KS-1692**.
- **The four platform suites did not run** (no local stack, no Docker for this seat) and **no real Redis was driven** — the gate's probes used a fake too.

## Next
An auth deploy carries this; it has not happened.

## BLUF
**Gate BO1 returned NO GO on the first head with one blocker, and it was right. Round 2 is pushed to the same PR #1655, head `893506989ae7c656e69408d4a6489b052b728e33`, READY FOR DELTA GATE, tier 1.** The reset route failed OPEN when the session store could not revoke: `revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0 with no throw** when Redis is unreachable, so the route wrote the password, burned the single-use token and answered 200 — and the old sessions validated again once Redis recovered. Both routes now fail closed on **both** sides of the write. Three tickets filed from the gate's notes. Nothing deployed.

## Recommendation
Delta-gate `893506989ae7c656e69408d4a6489b052b728e33`. This is round 2 of 2 under the cap, so a second NO GO ships nothing and goes to Kam. Merge on a GO naming that head; then an auth deploy, which has not happened.

## The blocker, and why my first body under-stated it
I had documented the case where the revocation **throws**. The real failure is quieter: `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318` is `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;` — a silent zero. The route logged `sessionsRevoked: 0`, indistinguishable from an account that had no sessions. **The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere** (`createSession`, `:156`), and that inconsistency is the root.

## The fix
Route-local, fail closed before the write **and** re-asserted after the revoke:
- **before the write** — store unavailable → 503, nothing written, the reset token **not** burned;
- **after the revoke** — re-assert, because the pre-write check alone is a check-then-act and the store dropping inside that window reproduces the defect exactly. Reset leaves the token **unburned** so a retry finishes the job; change-password says the password **WAS** changed, because telling that caller it failed would send them back to a password that no longer works.

`isRedisAvailable()` was already exported and `ServiceUnavailableError` already existed, so **`services/session.ts` is untouched** — deliberately. `revokeAllUserSessions` has exactly two other product callers (the user-erasure subscriber at `userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` and the admin status change at `routes/users.ts:838`), and changing its contract changes both; that is a wider ruling and is filed as KS-1692.

## Evidence
- **9 new cells** over two new files pin both halves of the failure mode, which no cell covered before. Each file carries a healthy-store positive control, and change-password carries an inverted-want control on the wording.
- **Red-proof, 5 arms**, each anchor proved unique, type-checked (an arm that will not compile is inadmissible, not a result), restored by content with a sha256 assert:
  - **A1′** the exact pre-fix product (guards *and* imports reverted) → **7 of 9 red**;
  - **A2** pre-write guards removed → 7 of 9;
  - **A3** only my **post-write re-assert** removed → **4 of 9 red**, which is what justifies that addition by measurement rather than argument;
  - **A4** the message reworded to claim failure → the inverted-want control fires;
  - **A5** `.catch(() => 0)` → **nothing red**, a negative arm that documents a real gap: these cells do not cover a *throwing* revoke.
- **Whole `services/auth` suite: 103 files / 1119 tests / 0 failed, 0 skipped.** Baseline on a clean checkout of the base: 99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed. +23 cells, **0 vanished**. `tsc` rc 0.
- **Four cell files now declare a healthy session store, one line each, with no assertion changed** — proved by identical `expect(` and cell counts before and after. Two of them (`ks1005`, `ks1052`) **predate this PR** and were found by running the whole suite rather than by reading the route: 6 cells there pin the happy path of both doors without declaring the store's state. Neither is a defect in those tests; the product now has a precondition it did not have.
- Preflight, quoted as printed: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` Legs 3, 4, 8 need a local stack. Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files: **154 examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.
- Push rc 0, 623s, a **fast-forward** `8e5308a87..893506989` — `origin` was proved an ancestor beforehand, so the hook's non-fast-forward refusal was satisfied, not bypassed.
- Landing on live develop predicted **`2346900a5105fe24f8b3777a73123dd6df80a2a5`**, merge-tree rc 0, exactly 8 files. Develop moved 6 commits during the round; its advance is 9 files with **0 overlap** with mine (negative control 9).

## Tickets filed from the gate's notes
- **KS-1690** (Bug, High) — the OAuth `refresh_token` grant never reads `decoded.sessionId`, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a new session (gate measured 200 twice, 2 live sessions). Scoped to the origin-session half: **KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of that branch and is still open.** Overlapping but distinct; neither should be closed as a duplicate of the other.
- **KS-1691** (Bug, Medium) — an in-flight request resurrects a revoked session, which is then missing from `user_sessions:<id>` so a second revoke returns 0 and cannot reach it.
- **KS-1692** (Bug, High) — the silent zero as it reaches the erasure subscriber and the admin path.

## Still not covered
- **The four platform suites did not run** (no local stack, no Docker for this seat). This touches a runtime surface, so that is a real gap.
- **No real Redis was driven** — the gate's probes used a fake too.
- **N5** (a login straddling the write) is reasoned, not run, and left as residue.
- **N-1382-2** untouched, which is why this stays `Refs`.
- No migration, schema or config change.

## BLUF
**N-1382-1 is BUILT and raised as PR #1655 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1655), head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`, READY FOR GATE, tier 1.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions. **The behaviour change a reviewer must agree to: change-password revokes the caller's OWN session, so the client must sign in again.** Nothing is deployed. N-1382-2 stays open, so this is `Refs`, not a close.

## Recommendation
Gate it as tier 1 — it is a session and credential surface, and it does not merge on a green run alone. Merge on a GO naming head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`; then an auth deploy, which has not happened.

## What changed
| door | file | placement | why there |
|---|---|---|---|
| change-password | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` (+3/-0) | after `updateUserOrThrow` | the write throws if it did not land, so a revocation can never follow a non-write |
| reset-password | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` (+4/-1) | after the write, **before** `consumeResetToken` | a revocation that throws leaves the single-use token **unburned**, so the user can retry instead of holding a changed password and a dead token |

`revokeAllUserSessions` is account-wide and nothing spares `req.sessionId`, so the caller's own access token stops validating after a successful change. That is deliberate. The alternative (`getUserSessions` + `revokeSession` minus the caller's own) needs two functions the existing session mock does not provide; it was neither built nor ruled.

If the revocation throws (a Redis fault) **after** the password was written, the request answers an error although the password did change. Reset: the token is unburned, so a retry works. Change-password: the user retries with the new password as the current one.

## Evidence
- **Red-first, reproduced here rather than quoted: 6 failed / 14 run** — 3 of 7 in each new cell file, the three RED assertion cells, with all 8 CONTROL cells green and 0 load-failure signatures. Green after: **14 passed / 14 run, 0 skipped**. `tsc --noEmit -p services/auth` rc 0.
- **`services/auth` suite, both ends measured on real trees:** baseline **99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed** on a clean checkout of the base; after **101 files / 1110 tests / 0 failed**. +14 cells, **0 vanished**.
- **13 mutation arms, 13 killed, 0 survivors, so no cell was added.** Including two that pin *which* account is revoked (revoke a different account id reds R1 on both doors). Each arm proved its anchor unique before tampering, type-checked (a mutant that will not compile is inadmissible, not a survivor), and restored by content with a sha256 equality assertion.
- **Who this breaks: nobody, measured.** No in-repo client calls either route. `me/change-password` has 8 hits, every one the route, the generated spec, the OpenAPI registration or a test; `auth/reset-password` has **zero** call sites under `frontend/` or `sdk/`. Controls: the same search shape finds `auth/login` in 6 files under `frontend/` and 105 repo-wide. `frontend/admin/src/pages/Profile.tsx:49` `handleChangePassword` posts to `/api/auth/password/reset-request` — it emails a reset link and never calls this route. Both SDKs expose no password or session surface. **Equally: no in-repo client exercises this behaviour at all.**
- Pre-push preflight, in-hook: **`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`** Legs 3, 4 and 8 need a local stack that was not up. Quoting it as the gate printed it, including its own line *"This is NOT a pass."* Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files against the ratchet baseline: **152 files examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.

## Not covered
- **The four platform suites (Schemathesis / Akto / Playwright / Performance k6) did not run** — they need the local stack, and this seat is held off Docker on this machine. This does touch a runtime surface, so that is a real gap, stated rather than skipped.
- **No real Redis was driven.** Both cell files replace the session service, so what is pinned is that the call is made, once, for the right account, at the right point in the sequence — not that Redis actually drops the sessions.
- **N-1382-2 untouched** — the e2e case at `tests/e2e/tests/security-bad-actor.prelaunch.spec.ts:1155,1182` posts to `/api/auth/change-password`, a route that does not exist.
- No migration, no schema change, no config or environment value.

The two patches are a local-model (Spark) pass applied byte-for-byte from each run's canonical `patch.diff`; the measurement above is mine.
